center.locator: Midpoint of the tunnel-walked CJPL-I and CJPL-II points
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure.

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: Jinping Mountain's surface above the tunnel; the two portal areas (west, near the Yalong River bend, and east) are about 8.4-8.8 km from the map centre. No feature is drawn at this level.

depth_m.note: Table I of this 2018 review gives BOTH CJPL-I and CJPL-II the same 2,400 m rock-burden/depth figure. The existing site:cjpl-ii record (not edited here) instead carries 2100 m from an earlier 2014 paper.
depth_m.quote: CJPL-I was built under Jinping Mountain with 2,400 m of rock overburden.

levels.name: Jinping traffic tunnel (~2400 m level)
levels.note: Houses geometry:jinping-traffic-tunnel, geometry:cjpl-i-point and geometry:cjpl-ii-point, all beside the same twin road-tunnel pair.

name: China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL)
notes: No accelerator or beamline entity has facility_id: facility:cjpl (it is a passive underground laboratory, not an accelerator complex), so unlocated[] has nothing to list on that front; both of the facility's sites (site:cjpl-i, site:cjpl-ii) are drawn.

detector:pandax-4t's placement site_id is site:cjpl-ii; no independently sourced sub-position for PandaX-4T within the CJPL-II hall complex was found this session, so it shares geometry:cjpl-ii-point rather than getting its own feature (unlike CERN's CMS cavern point, which had its own published coordinate).

summary.plain: China's deepest underground physics laboratory, built beside a hydropower traffic tunnel more than two kilometres under Jinping Mountain in Sichuan. CJPL-I and the newer, larger CJPL-II sit half a kilometre apart along the same tunnel.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:cjpl. Both halls are drawn as points derived by walking the sourced portal-to-hall distances (8.7-9.2 km) along an OpenStreetMap trace of the Jinping traffic tunnel (two near-identical parallel bores; one is drawn). The tunnel's own OSM-measured length (17.5 km) is cross-checked against the facility's published '17.5-km-long traffic tunnels' figure.
